Title: Local Agent
Description: Download the portable MyDevTools Local Agent for Windows x64 and review its version, checksum, permissions and tray controls.
SeoTitle: MyDevTools Local Agent for Windows x64 — Download
Keywords: MyDevTools local agent, Windows x64 download, portable HTTP client companion, no account
PrivacyShort: The agent connects directly from your PC to the target; MyDevTools does not proxy requests
HeroTitle: Connect browser tools to your Windows PC
HeroDescription: The Local Agent gives selected MyDevTools tools an explicitly authorized capability on your machine. It is portable, account-free and controlled from the Windows tray.
SetupIntro: There is no installer. Keep the executable in a location you control and launch it when a supported tool asks for the agent.
Step1Body: Save the executable in a permanent folder. Moving or deleting it later affects autostart.
Step2Body: Open the executable. Windows may ask you to confirm running a downloaded app; administrator access is not required.
Step3Body: Enter the fresh code shown by the agent into the MyDevTools tool. Pairing grants only the capability that tool requests.
PermissionsIntro: The agent is not an account, remote service or general command runner.
PermissionAccount: No sign-up, login or MyDevTools cloud proxy.
PermissionInstall: No administrator rights, installer or Windows Service.
PermissionPairing: A rotating one-time code starts a time-limited browser session. The browser stores the connection token for up to 8 hours or until the agent restarts, but never stores the pairing code.
PermissionNetwork: It listens only on this PC. HTTP requests and ICMP probes go directly from the agent to the target. Private-network targets are blocked by default. Routers seen along a path are shown even when they use a private address.
TrayIntro: Closing the small window hides it; the tray icon opens it again.
TrayCode: View the version and current pairing code.
TrayAutostart: Autostart is opt-in and off by default. It uses your Windows user settings and the executable must remain in place.
TrayExit: Exit stops the local server and revokes active sessions completely.
CapabilityBody: This release supports explicitly paired HTTP requests and ICMP path traces. Each tool asks for its own named capability; pairing does not grant future capabilities automatically.
VerifyBody: This executable is not digitally signed; Windows SmartScreen may warn or block it. Do not disable Windows protection. Compare the SHA-256 value above with the downloaded file to check integrity; a matching hash is not a publisher signature.
